response.sql: WITH st AS (SELECT o.observstation, o.lunarstage, AVG(t.bandusagepct) AS station_avg FROM telescopes t JOIN observatories o ON t.observstation = o.observstation GROUP BY o.observstation, o.lunarstage) SELECT lunarstage, AVG(station_avg) AS avg_bandwidth_usage_pct, COUNT(*) AS station_count, COUNT(*) * 1.0 / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS station_fraction FROM st GROUP BY lunarstage

assumptions.assumption: Stations are counted only if they have at least one telescope, because the inner join drops everything else. The fraction's denominator is the total number of such stations across all phases. A station whose telescopes all have a missing bandusagepct is still counted, but it adds nothing to the average.
A NULL lunarstage forms its own group, which is how GROUP BY already treats it.

alternatives.interpretation: Count every observatory station, including those with no telescopes, in the station count and in the fraction's denominator. Bandwidth averages still use only matched telescopes.
alternatives.sql: WITH st AS (SELECT o.observstation, o.lunarstage, AVG(t.bandusagepct) AS station_avg FROM observatories o LEFT JOIN telescopes t ON t.observstation = o.observstation GROUP BY o.observstation, o.lunarstage) SELECT lunarstage, AVG(station_avg) AS avg_bandwidth_usage_pct, COUNT(*) AS station_count, COUNT(*) * 1.0 / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS station_fraction FROM st GROUP BY lunarstage
